presets.name: unoptimized
presets.label: unoptimized
presets.description: unoptimized builds (O0) — surfaces simple structural differences
presets.long_description: The UNOPTIMIZED dataset includes binaries that are compiled without optimizations and are stripped. These are the easiest targets in the benchmark.

presets.name: optimized
presets.label: optimized
presets.long_description: The OPTIMIZED dataset includes binaries that are compiled with O2 (or the equivalent on other compilers), with inlining disabled. This set is significantly harder and more representative of real-world binaries.

presets.name: inlined
presets.label: inlined
presets.long_description: The INLINED dataset includes binaries that are compiled with O2, with inlining enabled. This set is even harder than optimized binaries and represents the frontier of decompilation research.

presets.name: large
presets.label: large
presets.description: large functions only (upper size tail), optimized without inlining
presets.long_description: The LARGE dataset includes only large functions from the OPTIMIZED dataset, which have been shown to be difficult for decompilers. This group represents the functions that reverse engineers are most likely to have difficulty with.

presets.name: sample-set
presets.label: sample-set
presets.description: 250 frozen targets across optimizations and projects; coverage counts successful decompilations
presets.long_description: The SAMPLE-SET dataset is a sampled version of the entire benchmark (unoptimized, optimized, inlined, ...) meant to give decompiler developers a small but significant sample to improve upon. It also allows for cheaper runs for quick development. It is likely that a perfect score here will be a near-perfect score on all other datasets. WARNING: results from LLMs can be biased since this dataset is open-source and some LLMs have shown capability for perfect recall on assembly-only samples. See changelog for details.
